comment: Every test failure this repository currently expects, and why.
It exists because a step that is already red absorbs the next failure without trace.
TestGenerateCatalogIdempotent was red on main for two merges, inside a step red for the
ratchet; TestFirehoseSnowflakeSecretAndPersistentBuffer failed once inside the same step
and was invisible for the same reason. Neither was hidden cleverly. Both were hidden by a
scripts/known-red.sh reads a `go test` run and says which of its failures are on this list
and which are not. It does NOT make anything pass: every entry here is still a red test and
still fails its step. What changes is that the first line of the output says whether the red
is the one expected or a new one -- which is the whole difference between a gate and a colour.
An entry may be added only with a reason a reader can check, and removed the moment the test
goes green. TestKnownRedIsDeclaredHonestly enforces both halves: every entry must name a test
that exists in the tree and carry a non-empty reason.

expected.why: Deliberate, and the point of the ratchet: the baseline is the PRE-DRIFT target, not a floor to raise, and the tree exceeds it. It goes green by shrinking the tree, NEVER by running `ratchet -write`. It does NOT, however, go green by deleting azure/blobs, which this entry claimed until it was measured. Removing that pack brings exactly two of the six metrics to baseline -- packs 47 and register_sites 47 -- and leaves four over: services_loc 50840 against 45537 (+5303), fault_sites 942 against 754 (+188), case_labels 1767 against 1734 (+33), services_files 85 against 82 (+3). The baseline is an exact snapshot of internal/services at cd145fb6 (82 files, 45537 lines); the tree was already 5741 lines over by 2ec06ba4, the commit that restored this baseline after #367 re-pinned it to the drift. So the excess is the five packs C54 records arriving in one merge window, and deleting the last of them recovers only its own 241 lines. 649 of the residual is aws/eventhttp and aws/scheduleexpr: counted here because Measure walks every non-test .go under internal/services, but neither is a pack -- neither calls Register -- so neither appears in pack_dirs and nothing lists them as extraction targets. The rest is in the 47 packs pack_dirs does list, and comes out as those are extracted.

The other half of the same statement: ratchet.json is deliberately stale relative to the tree, for exactly as long as TestRatchetNotExceeded is red. It compares packs, case_labels, services_loc and fault_sites for EQUALITY, so it stays red until the tree is brought down to the baseline -- not until azure/blobs is deleted, which moves only packs. See that entry for the measured breakdown of what is left after it goes.
